text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Foreigners can own the entire equity in a Malaysian business provided they can export over 80 percent of its production, Minister for International Trade and Industry Rafidah Aziz said.

-- Pica (M) Corp Bhd is planning to become the first Malaysian company to launch a closed end mutual fund. It is expected to submit an application the the Securities Commission this week, its managing director Abdul Aziz Mohd Hussain said.

-- The study of Islamic civilisation will soon be a compulsory and standard subject in all public and private universities. Minister in the Prime Minister's department Abdul Hamid Othman said this was to help foster greater understanding between Moslems and non-Moslems in this multi-ethnic society.
-- Telekom is planning to increase its stake in Thai telephone company Samart Corp Plc by another five percent. It recently acquired 20.12 percent of Samart's equity for $71.5 million.

-- Tenaga Nasional Bhd will invest one billion ringgit in Cyberjaya, an intelligent township being built outside Kuala Lumpur, for distribution of electricity, its chairman Tajuddin Ali said. Cyberjaya is part of a 15-by-50 km zone for high technology companies.
-- Talam Corp Bhd said it expects to start work on a 260-km West Coast highway early next year. The project would cost six billion ringgit and would be operated by the company for 35 years.
